messages:
Maya L: Kicking off an apples-to-apples run to isolate KV warmup noise + batching heuristics on the quantized 13B (q4_0) profile. Goal: measure p50/p95 latency, tokens/s, and speculative decoding hit rate for replay vs synthetic traffic. Will pin kernel selection to `auto` vs `force_xform`.

Jamal K: Nice. Which replay set and synthetic distrib are you using? also share the run config pls.

Maya L: Using replay: `2026-02-infra-queries-replay` (mixed seq len, ~15% short tail). Synthetic: Poisson arrival with lambda tuned to emulate the same seq length distribution. Config: 
```
MODEL=q13b-q4_0
KERNEL=auto
BATCH_WINDOW_MS=8
MAX_BATCH_TOKENS=4096
KV_CACHE=WARMUP_ON
SPECULATIVE=enabled
REPLAY_SET=2026-02-infra-queries-replay
SYNTH=poisson:lambda=0.9
RUN_SEED=42
```

Li Chen: FYI we saw KV warmup inflate p95 when warmup requests are included. Are you removing the first 300s of runtime for warmup?

Maya L: Yes removing 5m warmup. Also running a variant with KV_CACHE=warmup_off to quantify the delta.

PerfBot: Run 1767894321-1 complete. Summary: replay p50=42ms p95=220ms tokens/s=18.2 spec-hit=0.68. synthetic p50=40ms p95=180ms tokens/s=19.0 spec-hit=0.71. CI spread (n=5) tail sd ~12ms. Full log: link://perf/1767894321-1

Jamal K: Interesting gap on p95. Could be kernel selection reacting differently to sequence variance. Can you rerun with `KERNEL=force_xform` and `BATCH_WINDOW_MS=4` to check micro-batching sensitivity?

Maya L: Rerun started. Also instrumented kernel choice trace and KV hit histogram.

PerfBot: Run 1767894321-2 complete. Summary: replay p50=44ms p95=190ms tokens/s=17.5 spec-hit=0.66. synthetic p50=39ms p95=170ms tokens/s=18.8 spec-hit=0.70. Kernel trace shows 62% `xform` kernels on replay vs 47% on synthetic. KV hit histogram: warmup_off reduces early p95 by ~30ms but steady-state similar.

Li Chen: Looks like replay's tail is driven by long-tail kernel path + occasional KV miss storms during bursts. Could test adaptive batching: `BATCH_WINDOW_MS=adaptive` with target latency 60ms.

Sarah T: From a regression-gate POV, we discussed allowing up to 0.8% quality drop (eval set) for a 20% token cost win. What's the measured quality delta for q4_0 + speculative=enabled here?

Maya L: Ran micro-evals on the held prompt set: quality delta ~0.3% (BLEU-like proxy) vs baseline fp16. Speculative decoding changed token distribution slightly; no regression alerts triggered by eval harness.

OpsBot: Noted cluster noisy neighbor during run 2 at 1767894405 — saw 12% CPU steal on host-03 for ~20s. treat that as flagged noise in logs.

Jamal K: Given noise, next steps: 1) rerun pinned kernels + adaptive batching, 2) replay with trimmed ultra-long tails (>512 tokens) to match synthetic, 3) add deterministic KV-warmup phase (fixed seed).

Maya L: Agree. I'll schedule runs and add a follow-up thread with condensed numbers. For gating, propose: block on any config that increases p95 by >10% or quality drop >0.6%. Otherwise prefer configs that reduce tokens/s cost by >=12% with quality <=0.5% delta.

Li Chen: +1 to gate thresholds. Also add a metric for spec decoding hit rate <0.5 -> fail, since when spec-hit is low it increases wasted compute.

Maya L: Ack. I will attach the kernel traces and KV histograms in the follow-up. Thanks all :party_parrot:
